config.title: Race Condition Fix

intro.title: Race Condition Fix
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue app that fetches user data from a mock API to demonstrate and fix a race condition. You will learn how race conditions occur when multiple asynchronous operations compete, leading to unpredictable results. The main technologies involved are Vue's reactive state, the Composition API with ref, and asynchronous JavaScript using async/await. By the end, you will implement a fix using a cleanup function to ensure only the latest API response updates the UI.
intro.usecase: Race conditions frequently occur in modern web applications where multiple asynchronous operations compete for shared resources. In a dashboard application, this might manifest when users rapidly toggle between different date filters while charts are loading—causing outdated data to overwrite newer selections. Search interfaces with type-ahead suggestions can display results for stale queries if new requests complete out of order. Properly handling these scenarios ensures users always see accurate, consistent data regardless of interaction timing.

objectives: Implement a reactive data property to track the loading state of an asynchronous operation
Apply conditional rendering to display a loading indicator while data is being fetched
Construct a method that prevents duplicate API calls by checking the current loading state
Configure a watcher to trigger data fetching when a reactive dependency changes
Update component logic to cancel pending requests when new requests are initiated
Bind user interactions to methods that safely trigger asynchronous operations
Control the sequence of asynchronous operations to ensure data consistency
